answer.policy_title: Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 for Shoulder Arthroscopy
criteria_quotes: History of an acute event of instability (subluxation or dislocation) or acute onset of pain following activity
Clinical exam findings demonstrate positive apprehension test, positive relocation test, positive labral grind test, or objective laxity with pain
Range of motion is not limited by stiffness upon physical exam (PE is not required if there has been a recent episode of instability)
Labral tear/Bankart lesion on MRI or CT imaging
Minimal to no evidence of degenerative changes on imaging
Recurrent instability (subluxation or dislocation) with at least 2 instability events
Labral tear on MRI or CT, with/without bony Bankart fracture not > 25% of glenoid width upon imaging
answer.submission_route: Mailed to: Ambetter from Sunflower Health Plan, Attn: Appeals and Grievances Department, PO Box 10341, Van Nuys, CA 91410. Alternatively, faxed to 1-833-886-7956, or submitted over the phone by calling Member Services at 1-844-518-9505 (TTY 711).
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The policy is publicly available. If the patient needs to obtain a hard copy of the criteria directly from the plan, they can contact Ambetter from Sunflower Health Plan Member Services at 1-844-518-9505 (TTY 711) or refer to the provider clinical policies online portal.
answer.notes: The prior authorization for musculoskeletal (MSK) procedures under Sunflower Health Plan is managed by Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates, Inc. / NIA). CPT code 29806 (surgical shoulder arthroscopy capsulorrhaphy/instability repair) is governed by Evolent Clinical Guideline 1770 (historically NIA_CG_318). Under the 'Anterior-Inferior Labral Tear (Bankart Lesion)' section of this guideline, the imaging-specific necessity criteria (which must be met alongside clinical symptoms) require 'Labral tear/Bankart lesion on MRI or CT imaging' (or with a bony Bankart fracture not exceeding 25% of glenoid width for recurrent instability) accompanied by 'Minimal to no evidence of degenerative changes on imaging'.
